landmarks.name: Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary
landmarks.writeup: A sanctuary dedicated to the protection and rehabilitation of chimpanzees, promoting wildlife conservation.

landmarks.name: Bunce Island
landmarks.writeup: An important historical site, Bunce Island was a major slave trading post during the transatlantic slave trade.

landmarks.name: Freetown Cotton Tree
landmarks.writeup: A historic symbol in Freetown, believed to be the site where freed slaves first gathered upon arrival.

cultural_events.name: Freetown Music Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event showcasing local and international music, celebrating Sierra Leone's rich musical heritage.

cultural_events.name: Krio Heritage Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A festival celebrating the culture, language, and traditions of the Krio people.

food_writeup: Sierra Leonean cuisine features rice as a staple, often served with flavorful stews made from fish, meat, and vegetables, with popular dishes including groundnut stew and cassava leaves.
brief_history: Sierra Leone was founded in the late 18th century as a settlement for freed African American, West Indian, and liberated African slaves. It became a British colony in 1808 and gained independence in 1961. The country experienced a brutal civil war from 1991 to 2002 but has since been rebuilding.

important_people.name: Zainab Bangura
important_people.description: Former UN Special Representative on Sexual Violence in Conflict

current_conflicts: Sierra Leone is currently stable with no major internal conflicts, focusing on post-war recovery and development.
